items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: That’s my next question, but I just wanted to comment, parenthetically for the people listening to the interview, that they really must understand the tremendous importance of Down Beat to that world at that time.

Oh yeah. I used to – I had to review it, because it came in, but I never understood Charlie Ventura. I thought it was mainly playing notes at a hard tempo, and loud. One day his manager called me up and said, “What have you got personally against Charlie? You’re really hurting him economically.” I said, “I never met the guy.” In that sense I realized I had power. That’s what led to my brooding about it after a while.
Right. But, to stay there for a moment, you said “a regime of one.” What was the reality of the Down Beat office in 1950?
